grant: Title X Family Planning Services Grants
why: Strong fit: Title X directly funds family planning and preconception services under DPH, advancing G2.O4 reproductive and maternal health work.
main risk: The actual amount available will not be determined until enactment of the FY 2027 federal budget.

grant: Public Health Crisis Response Cooperative Agreement
why: Aligns with public health workforce surge staffing and DPH preparedness role; only creates an unfunded roster until CDC activates an emergency.
main risk: This NOFO only creates an approved but unfunded roster; actual funding is contingent on CDC determining a public health emergency exists and on future appropriations, so it may never result in award money.

grant: Home Study and Post-Release Services for Unaccompanied Alien Children​​
why: Fits G2.O2 child safety and permanency and state child welfare expertise in DSS, but serves a federal immigration-specific population with high ORR compliance demands.
main risk: NCDHHS does not have routine jurisdiction over unaccompanied alien children, and this ORR program is typically operated by nonprofits with immigration case management experience, making it an unfamiliar compliance-heavy program rather than a core state child welfare function.

grant: Emerging Infections Network - Research for Preventing, Detecting, and Managing Travel-associated Infectious Diseases
why: Strong fit for DPH disease surveillance and preparedness; CDC travel-focused sentinel network advances data-driven decision-making, though it is not squarely in NCDHHS strategic goals.
main risk: The international travel focus may exceed DPH's routine state-level disease surveillance authority and require coordination with federal quarantine stations, airports, or academic partners.

grant: NARMS Cooperative Agreement Program to Strengthen Antibiotic Resistance Surveillance in Retail Food Specimens
why: Funds antibiotic resistance surveillance in retail food; fits DPH lab and epidemiology role but is narrow and not a named NCDHHS objective.
main risk: Specialized FDA/NARMS retail food surveillance may require existing laboratory capacity and federal collaboration, so if NC is not already a NARMS retail food site the start-up effort could be high relative to the grant's narrow scope.

why: This FDA cooperative agreement funds state food testing laboratory capacity which fits DPH's public health laboratory and environmental health role though it is not tied to named NCDHHS strategic objective.
main risk: The opportunity may be limited to existing FDA-aligned food testing laboratories because it requires ISO 17025 accreditation and a valid 20.88 agreement with FDA prior to application.

grant: US Travelers Health Research, Surveillance, Communication, and Outreach Network
why: The CDC travel health surveillance network is a moderate fit for DPH infectious disease work but only indirectly supports NCDHHS data infrastructure and health access goals.
main risk: The announcement provides no eligibility, funding, or cost-sharing details, and NCDHHS does not currently operate a dedicated travel medicine program, so participating could require building new clinical and informatics capacity.

grant: Institute of Education Sciences (IES): National Center for Special Education Research (NCSER): Using Longitudinal Data to Support State Education Policymaking in Special Education, Assistance Listing Number (ALN) 84.324S
owner: Division of Child and Family Well-Being
why: Special education SLDS work is primarily DPI/SEA; NCDHHS fits only through early intervention and lacks the research/data-system role, so it is not a priority.
main risk: The core data and policy authority sits with the State educational agency, so NCDHHS would likely be limited to early intervention and would need significant research capacity to compete.

grant: Innovative Traffic Safety Enforcement (ITSE) Grant Program
why: Traffic safety enforcement falls under law enforcement/DOT, not NCDHHS health and human services; no division has authority or capacity to run it.
main risk: The grant would require NCDHHS to administer law-enforcement traffic safety programs that are outside its health and human services authority and divisional expertise.

grant: Authority to Accept Unsolicited Proposals for Research Partnerships Notice of Intent (NOI)
why: HUD housing-policy research does not fund NCDHHS health/human services priorities and requires a 50% match; low fit for any division.
main risk: The required 50 percent cost match makes a housing-focused research opportunity expensive for a health and human services agency with no clear division owner.

grant: HIV Care Grant Program - Part B States/Territories Formula and AIDS Drug Assistance Program Formula and AIDS Drug Assistance Program Supplemental Awards
deadline: forecast close 2026-10-30 (forecast post date passed - may already be open, check Grants.gov now)
why: Core DPH work: Ryan White HIV care and AIDS Drug Assistance Program funding advances G1 health access for low-income North Carolinians with HIV.
main risk: As a formula award, this may be an expected annual allocation rather than new discretionary funding, so the main burden is compliance and the amount is largely predetermined.

grant: Maternal, Infant, and Early Childhood Home Visiting Program (MIECHV)
owner: Division of Child and Family Well-Being
why: MIECHV directly funds home visiting that improves maternal and child health and birth outcomes; NCDHHS's Child and Family Well-Being division already runs home visiting, making this a strong fit.
main risk: The eligibility structure allows currently funded nonprofit organizations to apply if the state does not, so NCDHHS could lose state leadership or face incumbent competition.

grant: Strengthening Services to Prevent the Infectious Disease Consequences of Drug Use
why: Directly funds infectious disease testing and harm reduction for people who use drugs, fitting DPH disease prevention and G3.O4 substance use crisis priorities.
main risk: The biennial biobehavioral survey of people who use drugs requires specialized field data collection, privacy safeguards, and community partnerships that may exceed routine public health surveillance capacity.

grant: Preschool Development Grant Birth Through Five (PDG B-5) SMART Grant
deadline: forecast close 2026-11-17 (forecast post date passed - may already be open, check Grants.gov now)
owner: Division of Child Development and Early Education
why: One-year federal grant would fund early childhood data and technology infrastructure, directly supporting G5.O1 and fitting DCDEE's early learning data role.
main risk: The one-year, targeted nature may fund only a short-term build and not cover ongoing maintenance or broader statewide scale-up.

why: Funds HIV behavioral surveillance to track disparities and guide prevention, directly fitting DPH's existing disease surveillance and epidemiology role.
main risk: The program requires sustained field recruitment of hard-to-reach populations and delivery of HIV testing and linkage services, which may be operationally heavier than a typical data-only surveillance grant.
